description: Dependency policy shared by gokayo43's Bun projects.

minimumReleaseAge follows the slowest consumer's bunfig.toml, because a PR holding a version that repo's own window refuses fails its install. It moves to 3 days once every consumer's bunfig.toml holds releases for 3 days or less.
prBodyNotes: {{#if isVulnerabilityAlert}}This security fix skips the release-age wait, so `bun install` may refuse the fixed version as too new; [Vulnerability fixes](https://github.com/gokayo43/dev-config#vulnerability-fixes) has the steps that land it.{{/if}}

packageRules.description: Non-major updates land as one automerged PR per week.
Majors are read before they are merged.
This organisation's own releases skip the wait: the window holds back a stranger's compromised release, and these are ours. bun's window never holds them, since they install from git.
dev-config's and dev-config-db's pins carry executable gate code. Automerging one would land a gate that the adopting PR never showed anybody.
An Expo SDK is one release across every package it ships. A partial bump builds and then fails on a device, so the packages move together and a human reads the SDK's changelog before they do.
Better Auth's plugins are versioned in lockstep with the core; a plugin ahead of the core fails at import.

@oxlint/plugins publishes one version per oxlint release and describes that release's AST. The anti-slop rules are typed against it, so the two move together or this repo's typecheck grades the plugin against an AST oxlint is not handing it.

customManagers.description: Released binaries pinned by tag and archive SHA-256, which no built-in manager reads: in a run: block, or in the shared shell library that fetches a tool more than one caller needs. The renovate: comment above the pair names the dependency, so one manager covers every tool pinned this way — a YAML key or a shell assignment.
The same gitleaks pin appears unhashed in this repo's local install instructions.
